 Supplementary notes 

In the FBI’s Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program, violent crime is composed of four offenses: murder and nonnegligent manslaughter, forcible rape, robbery, and aggravated assault. Violent crimes are defined in the UCR Program as those offenses that involve force or threat of force.  
  
Due to the FBI's transition to a new crime reporting system, not all law enforcement agencies submitted crime data to the FBI. As a result, figures may not accurately reflect the total number of crimes and are not comparable to previous years' data.

## Life in the District

The District of Columbia has seen [fluctuating population](https://www.statista.com/statistics/206105/resident-population-in-district-of-columbia/) growth over the past few decades. Its population declined throughout the 1990s, when crime rates were at their peak, but has recovered since then. While [unemployment in the district](https://www.statista.com/statistics/189405/unemployment-rate-in-district-of-columbia-since-1992/) has also been falling, it still had a [high poverty rate](https://www.statista.com/statistics/205446/poverty-rate-in-the-district-of-columbia/) in recent years.

## Law enforcement in the U.S.

Crime rates in the U.S. have decreased compared to previous years, although many Americans still perceive crime as an important issue. The [number of law enforcement officers](https://www.statista.com/statistics/191694/number-of-law-enforcement-officers-in-the-us/) in the U.S. has recently increased. Additionally, initiatives by the Justice Department, focused on community-based prevention and intervention programs, have further helped lower violent crime rates.

 Supplementary notes 

In the FBI’s Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program, violent crime is composed of four offenses: murder and nonnegligent manslaughter, forcible rape, robbery, and aggravated assault. Violent crimes are defined in the UCR Program as those offenses that involve force or threat of force.  
  
Due to the FBI's transition to a new crime reporting system, not all law enforcement agencies submitted crime data to the FBI. As a result, figures may not accurately reflect the total number of crimes and are not comparable to previous years' data.

## Life in the District

The District of Columbia has seen [fluctuating population](https://www.statista.com/statistics/206105/resident-population-in-district-of-columbia/) growth over the past few decades. Its population declined throughout the 1990s, when crime rates were at their peak, but has recovered since then. While [unemployment in the district](https://www.statista.com/statistics/189405/unemployment-rate-in-district-of-columbia-since-1992/) has also been falling, it still had a [high poverty rate](https://www.statista.com/statistics/205446/poverty-rate-in-the-district-of-columbia/) in recent years.

## Law enforcement in the U.S.

Crime rates in the U.S. have decreased compared to previous years, although many Americans still perceive crime as an important issue. The [number of law enforcement officers](https://www.statista.com/statistics/191694/number-of-law-enforcement-officers-in-the-us/) in the U.S. has recently increased. Additionally, initiatives by the Justice Department, focused on community-based prevention and intervention programs, have further helped lower violent crime rates.

## Life in the District

The District of Columbia has seen [fluctuating population](https://www.statista.com/statistics/206105/resident-population-in-district-of-columbia/) growth over the past few decades. Its population declined throughout the 1990s, when crime rates were at their peak, but has recovered since then. While [unemployment in the district](https://www.statista.com/statistics/189405/unemployment-rate-in-district-of-columbia-since-1992/) has also been falling, it still had a [high poverty rate](https://www.statista.com/statistics/205446/poverty-rate-in-the-district-of-columbia/) in recent years.

## Law enforcement in the U.S.

Crime rates in the U.S. have decreased compared to previous years, although many Americans still perceive crime as an important issue. The [number of law enforcement officers](https://www.statista.com/statistics/191694/number-of-law-enforcement-officers-in-the-us/) in the U.S. has recently increased. Additionally, initiatives by the Justice Department, focused on community-based prevention and intervention programs, have further helped lower violent crime rates.

## Life in the District

The District of Columbia has seen [fluctuating population](https://www.statista.com/statistics/206105/resident-population-in-district-of-columbia/) growth over the past few decades. Its population declined throughout the 1990s, when crime rates were at their peak, but has recovered since then. While [unemployment in the district](https://www.statista.com/statistics/189405/unemployment-rate-in-district-of-columbia-since-1992/) has also been falling, it still had a [high poverty rate](https://www.statista.com/statistics/205446/poverty-rate-in-the-district-of-columbia/) in recent years.

## Law enforcement in the U.S.

Crime rates in the U.S. have decreased compared to previous years, although many Americans still perceive crime as an important issue. The [number of law enforcement officers](https://www.statista.com/statistics/191694/number-of-law-enforcement-officers-in-the-us/) in the U.S. has recently increased. Additionally, initiatives by the Justice Department, focused on community-based prevention and intervention programs, have further helped lower violent crime rates.

Wir verarbeiten Ihre Daten, um Inhalte oder Anzeigen bereitzustellen, und analysieren die Bereitstellung solcher Inhalte oder Anzeigen, um Erkenntnisse über unsere Website zu gewinnen. Wir geben diese Informationen auf der Grundlage einer Einwilligung an unsere Partner weiter. Sie können auf der Grundlage eines der folgenden bestimmten Zwecke oder auf Partnerebene über den Link unter jedem Zweck Ihr Recht auf Einwilligung ausüben. Diese Entscheidungen werden an unsere Anbieter, die am Transparency and Consent Framework teilnehmen, signalisiert.

#### Erforderliche Cookies

Immer aktiv

Diese Cookies, sind zur Funktion der Website erforderlich und können in Ihren Systemen nicht deaktiviert werden. In der Regel werden diese Cookies nur als Reaktion auf von Ihnen getätigte Aktionen gesetzt, die einer Dienstanforderung entsprechen, wie etwa dem Festlegen Ihrer Datenschutzeinstellungen, dem Anmelden oder dem Ausfüllen von Formularen. Sie können Ihren Browser so einstellen, dass diese Cookies blockiert oder Sie über diese Cookies benachrichtigt werden. Einige Bereiche der Website funktionieren dann aber nicht. Diese Cookies speichern keine personenbezogenen Daten.

Alle von diesen Cookies erfassten Informationen werden aggregiert und sind deshalb anonym. Wenn Sie diese Cookies nicht zulassen, können wir nicht wissen, wann Sie unsere Website besucht haben.

#### Erforderliche Cookies

Immer aktiv

Diese Cookies, sind zur Funktion der Website erforderlich und können in Ihren Systemen nicht deaktiviert werden. In der Regel werden diese Cookies nur als Reaktion auf von Ihnen getätigte Aktionen gesetzt, die einer Dienstanforderung entsprechen, wie etwa dem Festlegen Ihrer Datenschutzeinstellungen, dem Anmelden oder dem Ausfüllen von Formularen. Sie können Ihren Browser so einstellen, dass diese Cookies blockiert oder Sie über diese Cookies benachrichtigt werden. Einige Bereiche der Website funktionieren dann aber nicht. Diese Cookies speichern keine personenbezogenen Daten.

#### Werbe-Cookies

Alle von diesen Cookies erfassten Informationen werden aggregiert und sind deshalb anonym. Wenn Sie diese Cookies nicht zulassen, können wir nicht wissen, wann Sie unsere Website besucht haben.

Violent crime rate per 100k population by state (2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_violent_crime_rate#cite_note-FBI_2022-1)

This is a list of U.S. states and territories by violent crime rate. It is typically expressed in units of incidents per 100,000 individuals per year; thus, a violent crime rate of 300 (per 100,000 inhabitants) in a population of 100,000 would mean 300 incidents of violent crime per year in that entire population, or 0.3% out of the total. These data have been taken from the [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBI "FBI")'s [Uniform Crime Reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_Crime_Reports "Uniform Crime Reports").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_violent_crime_rate#cite_note-FBI_2022-1)

In the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), violent crime consists of five types of criminal offenses: [murder and non-negligent manslaughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homicide "Homicide"), [rape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rape "Rape"), [robbery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbery "Robbery"), [aggravated assault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aggravated_assault "Aggravated assault"), and [gang violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gang_violence "Gang violence").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_violent_crime_rate#cite_note-2)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Violent_Crime_by_State_2023.png/500px-Violent_Crime_by_State_2023.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Violent_Crime_by_State_2023.png)

Violent crime rate per 100k population by state (2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_violent_crime_rate#cite_note-FBI_2022-1)

This is a list of U.S. states and territories by violent crime rate. It is typically expressed in units of incidents per 100,000 individuals per year; thus, a violent crime rate of 300 (per 100,000 inhabitants) in a population of 100,000 would mean 300 incidents of violent crime per year in that entire population, or 0.3% out of the total. These data have been taken from the [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBI "FBI")'s [Uniform Crime Reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_Crime_Reports "Uniform Crime Reports").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_violent_crime_rate#cite_note-FBI_2022-1)

In the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), violent crime consists of five types of criminal offenses: [murder and non-negligent manslaughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homicide "Homicide"), [rape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rape "Rape"), [robbery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbery "Robbery"), [aggravated assault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aggravated_assault "Aggravated assault"), and [gang violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gang_violence "Gang violence").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_violent_crime_rate#cite_note-2)

For 2023, which US state was among the ten with the largest violent crime rates, the ten with the largest property crime rates, and the ten with the largest increase in poverty rate between 2022-2023?
